reader_summary: I can explain how one language assistant receives actual picture and sound data, and why fitting the input dimensions does not prove it uses either source. The picture is reduced to 48 color values and the sound to 16 frequency-band values, then each summary becomes one 64-number context feature. The short code checks an untrained model with a supplied example answer. The reported trained results need a separate reading: blue-only validation color scores can be won by a constant guess, balanced pitch scores are more informative, and successful color/pitch joint answers say nothing about shape. The changed-picture table makes the shape failure understandable: always answering circle gets the swapped circles right but still fails the original-square half of every pair. I could predict and complete the image-only exercise. No comprehension blocker remained.

terminology.details: RGB means three color channels, and the shape (3,16,16) is one picture rather than three pictures, as 10.1 explains. Modality is an information source such as image or sound, from 12.12. DIRECT is an answer marker and EOS is the ending ID, from 19.1. SFT learns assistant-answer positions; joint subsequently mixes text, pictures and sound; DPO is a later preference-comparison branch, from the target and 19.4. The target explicitly disambiguates task == joint from the training stage joint. Logits are candidate-ID scores at each position, labels are the next-position targets, and IGNORE exempts a position from the answer loss rather than removing its context. Counterfactual comparison is defined locally as changing an answer-relevant input while retaining the question and checking against updated truth. The only incomplete term background I found was the nonblocking log-mel link issue recorded above.

examples.details: I understand the relative pitch labels: this capstone groups tones near 440 Hz as low and near 880 Hz as high, while the earlier 300 Hz rule called 440 Hz high. They are different task definitions. In validation, a constant blue answer can earn color 9/9, whereas always guessing one pitch earns only 3/6 because the two classes are balanced. Joint 18/18 requires color and pitch, not shape. The DPO example changes blue,low to red,low, so pitch can stay correct while the whole answer fails; four such errors explain 18/18 becoming 14/18. In final image swaps, original successes total 9+0+18=27 of 36, changed successes total 9+9+18=36 of 36, and both-ends successes remain 27 of 36. Always saying circle explains the zero successful shape pairs despite 9/9 swapped-circle answers. These are my readings and arithmetic checks of cited earlier experiments; I did not rerun their trained-model evaluations.

program_explanation.details: build_dataset supplies a dictionary of train/other records and a second summary value; assigning the second to _ leaves it unused. The generator in next picks the first row whose task is joint. The printed user and answer let me see the question and demonstration before modality_tensors constructs the actual pixels and acoustic values from the record. CapstoneModel() is random and untrained. prepare_batch([row]) forms a one-record input dictionary and next-ID targets. Expanding **batch supplies ids, valid, images and audio_features as named arguments. Under torch.no_grad the forward call obtains logits without saving a derivative graph; it neither updates weights nor generates its own complete answer. The first two logits axes are batch and sequence position, aligned with labels; the third contains 264 possible next IDs. I ran the exact fenced Python on CPU and observed the joint question 圖片顏色與聲音高低？ with demonstration DIRECT:blue,low, image (3,16,16), sound (16,), logits (1,82,264), and alignment True. The varying middle length was not supplied by the prose, but no fixed middle length was needed to understand or predict the check.

exercise.details: Before execution I predicted that selecting image_color keeps the image dimensions but makes modality_tensors return audio=None, so the print must test for None before accessing .shape. I changed only the task selection and guarded that print, then added diagnostic prints. The run showed question 圖片是什麼顏色？, demonstration DIRECT:blue, image (3,16,16), acoustic summary None, logits (1,71,264), and alignment True. I initially expected batch audio_features itself might also be None; the real output disproved that extra assumption. A saved follow-up prediction and short public-API inspection resolved it: the batch has an all-zero (1,16) acoustic storage field, one image marker, and zero audio markers. Thus missing raw audio and a batch placeholder are different, while no sound context position is supplied. The exercise is actionable and does not ask the untrained model to recognize colors.

numbers_and_symbols.image_summary: 16x16 is the original height/width. Averaging to 4x4 RGB color blocks leaves 4x4x3=48 scalar values.
numbers_and_symbols.sound_summary: 16 denotes frequency bands; averaging across time leaves one energy summary for each band and discards order. 440/880 Hz denote about 440/880 cycles per second in this synthetic task.
numbers_and_symbols.context_projection: Each modality summary is converted to a 64-component feature occupying one context position, whereas the linked older expansion inserts multiple positions.
numbers_and_symbols.candidate_axis: 264 is the number of candidate next IDs. I need its role as the final logits-axis length, not a derivation of the vocabulary design, to read this check.
numbers_and_symbols.scores: x/y means x answers meeting the full criterion out of y tested answers; x/y pairs requires the original and changed answer both correct. Whole joint success requires both comma-separated components.
